## Andreev Bound State + Spin Orbit {.section-title}

:::: {.two-col .middle}
::: {.col}
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/media-p.slid.es/uploads/2455817/images/12905492/image.png){.abs-diagram}

E_J \cos(\varphi)

$$

::: {.citation}
Superconducting Spin Qubits, C. Padurariu & Y. Nazarov, 2009
:::

## Andreev Spin Qubit {.section-title}

::: {.center-stage}
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/media-p.slid.es/uploads/2455817/images/12905484/image.png){.asq-device}
:::

$$
\propto \frac{dE(\varphi)}{d\varphi}
$$

::: {.callout-text}
Spin degree of freedom couples to supercurrent!
:::

## Andreev Spin Qubit Readout {.section-title}

:::: {.two-col .middle}
::: {.col}
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/media-p.slid.es/uploads/2455817/images/12905508/image.png){.readout-img}
:::

::: {.col .state-labels}
$$\lvert 0\rangle$$

$$\lvert 1\rangle$$
:::
::::

::: {.callout-text}
Spin degree of freedom couples to supercurrent!

Thus, if we can measure supercurrent, we can do **readout**.
:::

::: {.citation}
Coherent manipulation of an Andreev spin qubit, M. Hays et al. 2021
:::

## Inductance Couples To The ASQ Ground State {.section-title}

::: {.center-stage .inductance-layout}
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/media-p.slid.es/uploads/2455817/images/12905492/image.png){.abs-diagram-rotated}
:::

$$
E_L \propto \frac{1}{L} \propto \frac{d^2E(\varphi)}{d\varphi^2}
$$

::: {.callout-text}
We can infer the ASQ state by measuring its inductance.
:::

## Why Are ASQ Challenging? {background-color="rgba(255, 242, 204, 0.53)" .question-slide}

::: {.big-question}
Why are ASQ challenging?
:::

::: {.challenge-list}
Material challenges:

- InAs nanowires usually have nuclear spins (phase decoherence)
- Graphene has no spin-orbit coupling
- Other materials are not reliable
:::

## Kramers' Theorem {background-color="rgb(217, 234, 211)" .section-title}

::: {.theorem-text}
Eigenstates of a **time-reversal symmetric** system with **half-integer spin** come in degenerate pairs.
:::

## Kramers' Theorem At TRS Flux {background-color="rgb(217, 234, 211)" .section-title}

::: {.theorem-text}
At fluxes $\varphi = 0,\pi$, the eigenstates of the Hamiltonian are degenerate.
:::

::: {.center-stage}
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/media-p.slid.es/uploads/2455817/images/12905484/image.png){.asq-half}
:::

::: {.callout-text}
Therefore, we need a magnetic field or a drive to implement gates.
:::

## Design: ASQ In A Network Of Inductors {.section-title}

:::: {.two-col .middle}
::: {.col}
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/media-p.slid.es/uploads/2455817/images/12905539/image.png){.network-img}
:::

::: {.col}
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/media-p.slid.es/uploads/2455817/images/12905541/image.png){.network-img}

$$
\lvert 1_L\rangle,\quad \lvert 0_L\rangle
$$
:::
::::

$$
H_{\sigma} =
J_{12}\sigma_{1,z}\sigma_{2,z}
+ J_{23}\sigma_{2,z}\sigma_{3,z}
+ J_{13}\sigma_{1,z}\sigma_{3,z}
$$

::: {.callout-text}
Kramers theorem forces a degenerate computational space at TRS flux.
:::

## Dispersive Readout Via Network Inductance {.section-title}

:::: {.two-col .middle}
::: {.col}
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/media-p.slid.es/uploads/2455817/images/12905539/image.png){.network-img}
:::

::: {.col}
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/media-p.slid.es/uploads/2455817/images/12905541/image.png){.network-img}
:::
::::

$$
H_{\sigma} =
J_{12}\sigma_{1,z}\sigma_{2,z}
+ J_{23}\sigma_{2,z}\sigma_{3,z}
+ J_{13}\sigma_{1,z}\sigma_{3,z}
$$

$$
H_r =
\hbar\omega_{r,0}a^\dagger a
+ \sum_{i\neq j}\hbar\chi_{ij}\sigma_{i,z}\sigma_{j,z}a^\dagger a
$$

::: {.callout-text}
A single readout resonator detects bit flips.
:::

## Dispersive Readout Via Network Inductance {.section-title}

::: {.center-stage}
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/media-p.slid.es/uploads/2455817/images/12906560/image.png){.readout-spectrum}
:::

$$
H_{\sigma} =
J_{12}\sigma_{1,z}\sigma_{2,z}
+ J_{23}\sigma_{2,z}\sigma_{3,z}
+ J_{13}\sigma_{1,z}\sigma_{3,z}
$$

$$
H_r =
\hbar\omega_{r,0}a^\dagger a
+ \sum_{i\neq j}\hbar\chi_{ij}\sigma_{i,z}\sigma_{j,z}a^\dagger a
$$

## Logical Gates {.section-title}

::: {.gate-list}
- <span class="gate-label">R<sub>x</sub>(&theta;)</span> using EDSR to drive each spin
- <span class="gate-label">R<sub>z</sub>(&theta;)</span> using adiabatic flux detuning
:::

::: {.drive-equation}
$$
U_{\sigma} =
E_J \cos(\phi)
+ E_{\sigma}
\left(
[\vec{\epsilon}_{SO}
+ \delta\vec{\epsilon}_{SO}\cos(\omega t)]
\cdot\vec{\sigma}
\right)\sin(\phi)
$$
:::

::: {.phase-equation}
$$
\theta =
\hbar^{-1}\int_0^T dt
\left(
E_{\lvert 0_L\rangle}(\Phi_t)
- E_{\lvert 1_L\rangle}(\Phi_t)
\right)
$$
:::
